api:
<Oscilloscope data={samples} x={|s: &Sample| s.time} trigger={0.5} span={0.02}>
    <TrendSeries name="CH1" y={|s: &Sample| s.ch1} />
    <TrendSeries name="CH2" y={|s: &Sample| s.ch2} />
</Oscilloscope>
PropTypeDefault
datarequired
xFn(&T) -> f64: time, in secondsrequired
children<TrendSeries>: one channel eachrequired
triggerf64: the level the first channel must rise throughnone: free running
spanf64: how much time to show, from the triggerall of it
y_axisAxisConfiglabelled "Volts"
legend, tooltip, classas on <Trend>

With a trigger, the view starts at the first rising crossing of that level, found between samples, so a repeating wave stands still as data updates. The level is drawn as a dashed line.

examples.title: Triggered
examples.description: Two channels, starting at the first rising crossing of 0.5 V on CH1, 12 ms wide.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn triggered() {
    let data = use_signal(capture(250.));
    rsx! {
        <Oscilloscope data={data} x={|p: &Probe| p.time} trigger={0.5} span={0.012} class="h-72">
            <TrendSeries name="CH1" y={|p: &Probe| p.one} />
            <TrendSeries name="CH2" y={|p: &Probe| p.two} />
        </Oscilloscope>
    }
}
